chunks: So that when they come (before the Lord) He will say: 'Did you deny My signs without having understood them? Or what was it that you were doing?'
ai.seo_question: What are the two main reasons God cites for the denial of His signs in this verse?
ai.summary: In Surah An-Naml, this verse captures the divine interrogation at the Hour, where God questions whether the disbelievers rejected His signs due to ignorance or willful rejection. Shia exegesis emphasizes the dual failure here: a lack of comprehensive knowledge ('ilm) of the signs' depth and the specific deeds ('amal) that manifested their denial, linking intellectual negligence to practical disobedience. This highlights the Quranic principle that true faith requires both understanding and action, a theme central to Shia theological discourse on the relationship between gnosis and practice.
